job.style: a short story with Indian characters in everyday life

passage: Rohan and his friends were sitting in the park when they started discussing their school project on the Indian Constitution. Rohan explained that the Constitution is not just a list of rules imposed by the government on citizens, but a foundational document that defines the relationship between the people and the state. Meera added that it ensures no single branch of government holds absolute power, as the judiciary acts independently to interpret laws rather than assisting the executive branch. Kabir mentioned that India follows a federal system where both the Central and State governments derive their authority directly from the Constitution, meaning neither is a subordinate 'boss' to the other. Finally, they discussed Fundamental Rights, noting that while these rights protect citizens from arbitrary state power, they are not absolute; they come with reasonable restrictions to ensure everyone’s freedom is respected. Rohan concluded that the Constitution acts as a shield for the people, ensuring that the government remains accountable and that every individual lives with dignity within a structured, democratic framework.

items.evidence: Rohan explained that the Constitution is not just a list of rules imposed by the government on citizens, but a foundational document that defines the relationship between the people and the state.
items.q: Tina thinks the Constitution is only something the government forces on citizens. How does Rohan see it?
options: It defines how people and the state relate
It lists rules the government imposes on citizens
It binds citizens but not government ministers
It is a rulebook only for courts and judges
items.explain: Rohan says the Constitution is a foundational document defining the relationship between people and the state.

wrong.why: thinks the Constitution is just laws imposed on people
thinks ministers are above the Constitution
links the Constitution only to the judiciary mentioned nearby

items.evidence: Meera added that it ensures no single branch of government holds absolute power, as the judiciary acts independently to interpret laws rather than assisting the executive branch.
items.q: Meera says judges interpret laws independently. Why is this important for India's government?
options: It stops one branch from holding all power
It helps the Prime Minister pass new laws
It lets the President take every big decision
It lets judges make laws for the executive
items.explain: An independent judiciary makes sure no single branch of government holds absolute power.

wrong.why: thinks the judiciary helps the Prime Minister make laws
thinks the President takes all big decisions
confuses interpreting laws with making them

items.evidence: Kabir mentioned that India follows a federal system where both the Central and State governments derive their authority directly from the Constitution, meaning neither is a subordinate 'boss' to the other.
items.q: How are the Central and State governments related under India's federal system?
options: Each draws its power directly from the Constitution
The Centre is the boss of every State
Each State holds powers the Centre lends it
Each State obeys the President's own orders
items.explain: Both governments get authority directly from the Constitution, so neither is the other's boss.

wrong.why: thinks federalism makes the Centre the boss
thinks State powers are a loan from the Centre
thinks the President personally runs the country

items.evidence: Finally, they discussed Fundamental Rights, noting that while these rights protect citizens from arbitrary state power, they are not absolute; they come with reasonable restrictions to ensure everyone’s freedom is respected.
items.q: Aman claims his right to free speech lets him spread lies about a neighbour. What would the friends say?
options: Rights have limits so others stay free too
Rights let him do anything at any time
Rights apply only to people who own property
Rights protect the state from its citizens
items.explain: Fundamental Rights are not absolute; reasonable restrictions protect everyone's freedom, including the neighbour's.

wrong.why: thinks rights mean doing whatever you want
thinks only property owners have full rights
reverses who is protected from whom
